paragraphs.text: Green-white ( or GW ), also called Selesnya , is an allied color pair. Green ( ) and white ( ) share a philosophy of community and harmony; they are the mutual enemies of black ( ), the color of amoral self-interest. Green and white have more mechanical overlap than any other color pair: they the foremost colors of creatures and of power/toughness pumping, and they also share the evergreen keywords vigilance , indestructible , flash , and ward for mana ; artifact and enchantment destruction; enchantment synergies and the enchantress ability; and damage prevention. Green-white decks typically employ a go-wide strategy.

Green is the color accepting the natural order and white is the color of selfless altruism. As mutual enemies of black , they abhor selfish actions that threaten the collective group. Accordingly, green and white's alliance is about responsibility. Green feels beholden to the natural ecosystem, and white to the greater good.

When paired, green and white converge on the idea of community. Green-white believes that only by embracing one's role within the larger group can one find serenity and bliss. It draws strength in numbers and is constantly recruiting. Both colors also value faith and tradition. Green-white's reliance on collectivism is both a strength and a weakness. A group can be greater than the sum of its parts, and not easy to disrupt by striking down individual members. But green-white can also be inflexible and slow to change. It can also be unsympathetic toward individual suffering, especially when that suffering benefits the larger group.

Green and white's disagreements mirror the red-blue conflict of heart versus head. Green, an ally of red , follows its natural inclinations. White, an ally of blue , thinks rationally about how to build a just society. White is more cautious and reactive than green. Green also embraces predation and survival of the fittest , which goes against white's desire to look after the weakest members of society.
Examples of Green-white heroes include Ajani Goldmane and Huatli , while villains include Dromoka and Oba .

Green and white have the greatest mechanical overlap of any color pair; this makes hybrid cards ( ) easy to design for, but gold cards difficult. Green and white are the most creature-centric colors; white has the most creatures by volume, followed by green, which also has the biggest creatures. Green and white are also the foremost colors of power and toughness pumping. Green-white decks typically employ a go-wide strategy, overwhelming the opponent with a large number of creatures.
The following mechanics are shared by green and white.
These multicolored cards best exemplify the strengths of green and white:
Heroes' Reunion — combines the two colors' life-gaining abilities into a very efficient card
Aura Shards — one of the most powerful artifact/enchantment hate cards in the game
Autochthon Wurm — green's large power and toughness combined with white's benefit of producing many creatures
